To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the TagL protein is a novel PG-binding protein that is essential to the assembly of the T6S complex and the anchorage of the T6 secretion system to the bacterial envelope.
we have identified a sub-complext of the T6S system and have determined that one of the proteins in this sub-complex is anchored to the peptiodoglycan.
the type VI secretion machinery is anchored to the peptido-glycan by a specific domain of the TssL subunit and that this subunit interacts with the TssM and TssJ proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the assembly of the T6S system and its anchorage to the PG, a key step in the secretion process.
the identification of the T6S machinery components, their function and their role in bacterial physiology and pathogenesis.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the assembly of the T6S machine and its interaction with the cell envelope.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the T6SS has been anchored to the PG by the TagL protein.
we still have much to learn about the type VI secretion systems.
the type VI secretion is a fascinating and rapidly evolving secretion system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the T6SS is anchored to the PG layer via the TssL-TssM-TagL sub-complex.
the T6SS is anchored to the PG layer by TagL.
we have identified the first protein that is directly involved in the anchorage of the T6S to the bacterial envelope.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the T6SS is anchored to the PG layer, and that the PG-binding motif of TagL is conserved among all known T6SS systems.
the T6SS is anchored in the PG and that PG-binding is likely to be an important function for several T6SS proteins.
, although the T6SS is anchored to the inner membrane via the TssL subunit, the TssL-TagL-TssM sub-complex is anchored to the PG layer.
